title: chamaecytisus triflorus subsp. ciliatus
intro: Chamaecytisus triflorus subsp. ciliatus, commonly known as the Hungarian clover or wild pea, is a plant species belonging to the Fabaceae family. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including inflammation, digestive problems, and skin conditions, due to its numerous health benefits. The therapeutic actions of Chamaecytisus triflorus subsp. ciliatus include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which contribute to its potential in treating various diseases. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which have been shown to possess significant therapeutic effects.
